page.heroIntro: The occasions on which the Circle convenes. Each is built for a different kind of conversation.

detail.criteriaIntro: Every signature experience suits a particular frame of mind as much as a particular seniority.
detail.stepsIntro: A short sequence, so that the time in the room is spent well.

items.name: CEO Leadership Summit

photo.note: a summit stage or full room, shot wide.

items.summary: The Circle's principal gathering of the year.
items.intro: The one occasion on which the whole membership convenes. The programme is built from the questions members bring, and the value is as much in the margins as in the sessions themselves.

criteria.title: Ready to be in the room
criteria.body: The summit rewards presence. Members who attend fully take more from it than those who pass through.

criteria.title: Carrying a live question
criteria.body: The programme is assembled from what members are actually working on.

criteria.title: Open to being introduced
criteria.body: Introductions are made throughout, and are the part members most often remember.

criteria.title: Willing to contribute from the floor
criteria.body: Sessions are conversations. The audience is the panel.

steps.title: Confirm your place
steps.body: Places at the summit are held for members and released in order of confirmation. Confirming early secures the seat rather than the date.

steps.title: Submit your themes
steps.body: Members send the questions they want raised beforehand, so the programme is shaped by the room rather than presented to it.

steps.title: Arrive unhurried
steps.body: The most useful conversations tend to happen either side of the formal programme. Allow for them.

steps.title: Carry it forward
steps.body: Introductions made during the gathering are followed up by the Circle, so momentum is not left to chance.

items.name: Chairman's Majlis

photo.alt: A majlis setting with low seating and warm light
photo.note: a majlis setting — low seating, warm light.

items.summary: An evening of open conversation, in the majlis tradition.
items.intro: Held in the majlis tradition: seated in the round, no head of the table, and no agenda beyond the subject raised from the chair. Conversation moves where the room takes it.

criteria.title: Comfortable without structure
criteria.body: There is no running order. The evening finds its own shape.

criteria.title: Content to listen
criteria.body: The majlis works because not everyone speaks at once, and nobody is obliged to speak at all.

criteria.title: Respectful of the form
criteria.body: The tradition carries its own courtesies, and members are asked to observe them.

criteria.title: Present in person
criteria.body: The majlis is not held remotely. Attendance means being in the room.

steps.title: Confirm your place
steps.body: Places at the majlis are held for members and released in order of confirmation. Confirming early secures the seat rather than the date.

steps.title: Submit your themes
steps.body: Members send the questions they want raised beforehand, so the programme is shaped by the room rather than presented to it.

steps.title: Arrive unhurried
steps.body: The most useful conversations tend to happen either side of the formal programme. Allow for them.

steps.title: Carry it forward
steps.body: Introductions made during the gathering are followed up by the Circle, so momentum is not left to chance.

items.name: Executive Leadership Retreat

photo.alt: A retreat setting away from the city
photo.note: a retreat setting away from the city — landscape or lodge.

items.summary: Time away from the office, and from the role.
items.intro: A residential gathering held away from the working environment, where the distance is the point. Members arrive as themselves rather than as their title.

criteria.title: Able to step away properly
criteria.body: The retreat asks for uninterrupted attention, which is the hardest thing a chief executive can offer.

criteria.title: Looking beyond the quarter
criteria.body: Sessions are built for the questions that never reach the top of the agenda.

criteria.title: Comfortable in a small group
criteria.body: Numbers are kept low so that everybody is known by the end.

criteria.title: Open to changing your mind
criteria.body: Members tend to leave with a different question than the one they arrived with.

items.name: Future Leadership Forum
items.summary: For the generation preparing to take the chair.
items.intro: Convened for senior leaders approaching the top role, and for the members preparing them. The forum exists to shorten the distance between readiness and appointment.

criteria.title: Approaching the top role
criteria.body: Built for those close enough to see the seat, and to feel the weight of it.

criteria.title: Sponsored by a member
criteria.body: Attendance comes through a member who knows the candidate's work directly.

criteria.title: Willing to be candid about gaps
criteria.body: The forum is most useful to those prepared to name what they do not yet know.

criteria.title: Serious about the transition
criteria.body: This is a working session, not a networking occasion.

items.name: Elite Excellence Awards

photo.alt: An awards evening, room set formally
photo.note: an awards evening — a room set formally, before or during.

items.intro: An evening given to recognising leadership as judged by those doing the same work. Recognition is decided within the membership rather than by submission or nomination volume.

criteria.title: Judged by peers
criteria.body: Recognition carries weight because of who is giving it, not how it was applied for.

criteria.title: Nominated, not entered
criteria.body: There is no submission process. Members put forward the work they have seen.

criteria.title: Measured over time
criteria.body: Consideration reflects a body of work rather than a single year's result.

criteria.title: Received in company
criteria.body: The evening is held among the membership, and is not a public occasion.

items.name: International CEO Delegation

photo.alt: Arrival in another market, a skyline on approach
photo.note: travel or arrival — an airport, a skyline on approach.

items.summary: A delegation abroad, convened around a single market.
items.intro: A small group travels together to one market, with a programme built around meeting the people who actually operate in it. The delegation is convened for understanding rather than for ceremony.

criteria.title: Serious about the market
criteria.body: Delegations are for members with a real interest in the destination, not a general curiosity.

criteria.title: Able to travel with the group
criteria.body: The delegation moves together. The conversations between meetings matter as much as the meetings.

criteria.title: Prepared in advance
criteria.body: Members read the briefing before departure so that time on the ground is not spent on background.

criteria.title: Representing the Circle well
criteria.body: Members travel as guests of the market they are visiting, and are asked to conduct themselves accordingly.

items.name: CEO Private Dinners

photo.alt: Elegant private dining room set for an intimate dinner
photo.note: Intimate, warm interior. Anchors Signature Experiences.

items.summary: A small table, a single subject, no agenda beyond the conversation.
items.intro: A private table convened around one subject, kept small enough that a single conversation can hold. There is no programme and no speaker — only the people at the table.

criteria.title: At ease in a small room
criteria.body: The table is kept small deliberately, so that nobody is a spectator.

criteria.title: Interested in the subject
criteria.body: Each dinner is convened around one question. Members come for that question.

criteria.title: Discreet about what is said
criteria.body: Members are asked to treat the table as confidential. The terms are set out in the Trust Framework.

criteria.title: Willing to stay late
criteria.body: The most useful part of the evening is rarely the first hour.
